SMTO-GWT-0045 — A model start request didn't say how to start the model

GUID: 0897485b-a208-4575-87c4-a060f5d7bb64
Slug: managed-llm-command-required
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • Something asked this computer's Gateway to start an AI model with its older built-in starter but didn't include the command that starts the model. Nothing was started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If a script or tool you use started the model by contacting the Gateway directly, add the model's start command to its request. The older starter can't guess which program or model to run.
  2. Otherwise, ask SMTO in a conversation to start the local AI model on that computer. SMTO's Local AI tools start models from saved setups, so you don't need to type a command.
  3. Before starting, ask SMTO to show the model's status on that computer. If the model is already running, starting it again isn't needed.

What success looks like

  • The model's status on that computer shows it running.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that computer's Gateway. Don't resend the same empty start request; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GatewayService.llm_start rejected a managed model start (400) because its command field was empty after trimming; no process was started.

What this means

  • Managed-model startup normalized the supplied command and found it empty before attempting to start a process. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Managed-model startup normalized the supplied command and found it empty before attempting to start a process.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the startup command in the intended managed-runtime request, including whitespace-only values and its working directory.

How to fix it

  • POST /llm/start needs a non-empty command (for example the model server's serve command line), with optional cwd and conda_env. Fix the script or tool that sends it, check /llm/status first, and prefer the Local AI runtime operations, which start models from saved profiles.
  • Configure the intended supported model startup command on the Gateway host.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported nonempty command validates and the resulting owned model process is reported by its runtime.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
